method: 3D SIMP topology optimization (parts/picogk-catalog/bionic/topopt.py), then PicoGK smoothing and exact functional features
basis_note: Crash-relevant part, prohibited pending engineering. Interfaces and loads are NOT measured. The domain is the FVD commercial envelope 139 x 100 x 53 mm; the 3 mm rear plate is the F0 hypothesis; the front contact pad is the 60 x 38 mm F0 shell outline. Loads are the synthetic 15 kN mean crush force per support of evidence/engineering-screen.json (regression input, not a Porsche or regulatory case) plus assumed oblique directions. Compliance minimisation gives a stiff static load path, NOT a crush/energy-absorption design: progressive folding, force-displacement and crash behaviour are not modelled.

design.note: FVD50501700 envelope 139 x 100 x 53 mm, kept 1 mm inside so the smoothed members stay within it

solid.note: 3 mm rear plate on the body rail (F0 hypothesis, no mounting holes: interface not measured)
bumper-beam contact pad, 60 x 38 mm outline of the F0 crush shell, 4 mm thick

supports.note: rear face of the plate held on the body rail (bolting idealised as clamped)

load_cases.name: axial
load_cases.note: synthetic mean crush force 15 kN per support (evidence/engineering-screen.json synthetic_cases), axial on the front pad

load_cases.name: oblique_left
load_cases.note: 15 kN at an assumed 15 deg in plan (oblique/offset impact): 14490 N axial + 3880 N lateral

load_cases.name: offset_low
load_cases.note: 15 kN at an assumed 10 deg downward, on the upper half of the pad only (bumper beam riding up / offset contact): 14770 N axial + 2600 N vertical
